No deprecated expo packages, no React Native issues observed.

minor.issue: Calendar Call Spread template is misclassified as 'Diagonal Call Spread' because /api/chain/template picks the nearest-ATM strike independently for the near chain (short leg) and the far chain (long leg) — if the two chains have slightly different strike grids the strikes end up different and classify() returns Diagonal. Repro: POST /api/chain/template Calendar Call Spread, then POST /api/strategies WITHOUT strategy_type -> doc.strategy_type == 'Diagonal Call Spread'. Fix option 1: in chain.py _leg_from_chain for the Calendar case, pass the EXACT short strike (not S) and if that strike is not in the far chain, pick the long strike that matches rather than the nearest. Fix option 2: in classify(), when len(exps)==2 and strikes are close (within 5%), still call it a Calendar. The frontend DOES pass strategy_type (SaveStrategyReq.strategy_type) when building from a template, so UI is unaffected — only direct API callers see the issue.

action_items: (Low) Fix classify() or template to make Calendar Call Spread auto-classify correctly when strikes diverge slightly between near/far chains. Frontend is unaffected because SaveStrategy passes strategy_type explicitly.

(Nice-to-have) The ClosedHistory 'delete-closed-*' button uses a 4s armed state (good), but there is no visible countdown indicator — consider a subtle pulse or progress bar so users know they have a short window to confirm.

(Nice-to-have) admin-user-detail shows strategies.open[].expiration and name/ticker but no mark/pnl snapshot. For an admin inspecting a user, showing current live P&L of open positions would speed up support investigations.
critical_code_review_comments: strategies.py admin_user_detail() builds the sign-up entry with plan='trial' hardcoded. For users whose first plan_event already captured 'trial' at sign-up this is fine, but if a user was pre-created with plan='expert' (like lingesa4) the UI will show 'TRIAL via sign-up' as the oldest entry which is misleading. Consider: plan_hist.append({'plan': u.get('plan') or 'trial', ...}) OR drop the synthetic sign-up and rely purely on real plan_events (ensure every user has one at register time).

strategies.py history_insights() calls max()/min() on rows and uses r.get('final_pnl') or 0 — if ALL closed trades have final_pnl=0 or None the best/worst both pick the first row with the same value, which is OK but 'best' and 'worst' being identical can look odd. Minor UX quirk.
strategies.py classify() returns 'Diagonal' when len(exps)==2 and strikes differ even by 1 point. See minor backend issue above — tightening this heuristic would help auto-classification.

StrategiesList.tsx ClosedRow archive handler toggles archived state but doesn't optimistically update — onChanged() triggers full reload. On slower networks the row stays visible for 1-2s after tap, which is OK but a subtle 'archiving...' indicator or disabling the icon briefly would be nicer.

admin-user/[uid].tsx: when d.plan_history is long (>5 entries) there is no 'Show more' truncation. The admin can scroll but a dense history is wall-of-text. Low priority — most users will have ≤3 entries.

rca_of_issue: Minor Calendar Call Spread auto-classification bug — root cause is in chain.py chain_template(): the near-leg (short) is picked with `_leg_from_chain(c, 'Sell', typ, S, ...)` and the far-leg (long) with `_leg_from_chain(fc, 'Buy', typ, short['strike'], ...)`. _leg_from_chain picks the strike NEAREST to the target in the chain's actual strike grid — but near and far chains can have different grids (e.g., AAPL near may list $186 while far lists $185). The resulting legs have different strikes, so classify() returns 'Diagonal Call Spread' instead of 'Calendar Call Spread'. The frontend sidesteps this by passing strategy_type explicitly from the template name, so end-user UI is unaffected. Fix: either (a) if the far chain doesn't contain the short strike, scan calls for the closest match to short.strike with a +/- 1 strike tolerance before falling back, or (b) in classify() treat two-expiration spreads with strikes within ~1% as Calendars.
